??? quote "Dialogue"

    - The cart will roll. Hambone said so in his wobbling voice, which means it is true. Rehearsals at dawn tomorrow. Bring a cushion.
    - Three falls and a breath of quiet. I have rebuilt the whole first act around them. The words stay the same, of course. The words always stay the same.
    - The Old Barracks Troupe, *Player*. Juna's play, on a cart, every Walkout Day, the way it was first done. What do you want? Quickly. Everything is quickly.
        - *Choice:* Tell me about Juna's play.
        - *Choice:* How did you become director?
        - *Choice:* Who is in the troupe?
        - *Choice:* Nothing, thanks.
    - Juna Marrow wrote a comedy that poked fun at Selsior's grandees. The guild banned it, so she played it on a cart in the market square, and they hauled the cart away. A few weeks later three hundred people walked out of the gates behind her.
    - So every Walkout Day we play it on a cart, as it was first played. Quint reads the Charter in the square first, slowly, on purpose, and I time our first entrance to his very last word.
    - I joined at nineteen, pushing the cart. Hambone showed me how. Then I played Juna for nine years, and when Bellamy Stroud died, the troupe looked at me, and I looked back, and that was that. Thirteen years ago.
    - My father carried me on his shoulders to my first Walkout Day play. I have been giving notes ever since. Yours: stop slouching.
    - Dex, the grandee, fifteen years in the hat. Rue, our new Juna, who froze in the wings and then owned the stage. Pip, who writes when she thinks I am not looking. Piper, who writes far too many songs. Hambone and the cart, Thimble and the costumes, and Sprout, who knows every part by accident.
    - Exit stage left, *Player*. That way. No, the other left.
